mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Direct Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or Registrar of Companies in the investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative only: (A) Hague Apostille Contracting State: notarize the certified copy in the country of issuance; obtain an Apostille from the competent authority such as the Secretary of State or Ministry of Foreign Affairs; submit to Chinese authorities without consular legalization. (B) Non-Apostille State: notarize the document; obtain authentication from the local designated authority; submit to the Chinese Embassy or Consulate for Consular Legalization. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Direct Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry of the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative only: (A) Hague Apostille Contracting State: notarize the document; obtain an Apostille from the competent issuing authority; do not perform Consular Legalization. (B) Non-Apostille State: notarize the document; authenticate it before the local designated authority; then obtain Consular Legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are exclusive alternatives and must not be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE incorporator or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor, notarized by an authorized notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative only: (A) Hague Apostille Contracting State: notarize the board resolution and power of attorney; attach a Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority in the country of origin; no Chinese Embassy legalization is required. (B) Non-Apostille State: notarize the board package; authenticate through the local foreign-affairs channel; complete Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Never combine Apostille and Consular Legalization in one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or constitutional documents of the Direct Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry-certified copy or company secretary-endorsed copy of the investor's constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative only: (A) Hague Apostille Contracting State: notarize the certified constitutional documents; obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state; submit the apostilled set to Chinese authorities directly. (B) Non-Apostille State: notarize the certified constitutional documents; authenticate them through the local competent authority; then apply for Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. These are mutually exclusive routes and must not be used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Direct Foreign Investor's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's banking institution, signed by a duly authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative only: (A) Hague Apostille Contracting State: notarize the bank officer's signature and the bank seal; attach a Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the bank's home state; no Consular Legalization is required. (B) Non-Apostille State: notarize the bank reference letter; authenticate through the local designated authority; then obtain Consular Legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel, exclusive alternatives and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed UBOs, directors, legal representatives, senior managers, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence before incorporation and on a continuing basis. Screening must cover the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists including country-specific programs applicable to cross-border payment rails; China's domestic AML/CFT watchlists and suspicious transaction indicators issued by the People's Bank of China and the Financial Intelligence Unit; and domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons and their family members and close associates. Any positive match must be escalated to the AML compliance officer; enhanced continuous monitoring applies to high-risk jurisdictions; WFOE formation must be suspended until clearance is documented and approved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation - Market Entity Name Registration System (accessed through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and local municipal SAMR portals; verification via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier naming convention: administrative division + distinctive trade name (transliterated or selected in Chinese) + industry description + organizational form, ending with Limited Liability Company in Chinese equivalent form. A foreign investor's Latin-script name must be rendered through a permissible phonetic transliteration or a separately approved Chinese trade name; English-only names are not accepted as the statutory name. Parallel English names may be used commercially but only after the Chinese statutory name is registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the SAMR at the next higher level within 60 days of receiving the written rejection notice, or institute administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within 6 months. The appeal package must include the original rejection notice, the online application reference number, a written explanation of the proposed name's distinctiveness, supporting trademark or investor-name rights, and a revised name option. If rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, a prior written approval or no-objection letter from the relevant competent ministry must be obtained before refiling. The original name reservation cannot be extended; a fresh filing must be made.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address is generally not permissible for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise in China. Municipal SAMR offices, tax bureaus, and commercial banks require proof of a physical registered office through a valid lease agreement, a property ownership certificate or real-estate license, and in many cases written consent from the landlord. For the mobile utility software industry, a serviced office with an assigned room, physical signage, and actual staff presence may be accepted, but a PO Box, virtual meeting address, or mail-only service will be rejected at registration or during bank account opening and will jeopardize tax invoice issuance. The registered address must match the principal place of business and be verifiable on inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood is moderate during the first two years and especially within six months of registration; quantified risk is approximately 35% in year one, declining to below 15% after stable operations. Checklist: nameplate matching the registered Chinese name displayed at the door; original lease contract and rent payment vouchers matching the registered address; employees present during business hours; functional desks, computers, development equipment, and software tools; attendance records, bank statements, contracts, and tax filing records showing actual commercial substance; e-invoice issuance equipment and address correspondence records. Municipal SAMR and tax authorities may conduct unannounced physical inspections; if no physical presence is found, registration may be revoked, tax invoice quotas cancelled, and bank accounts frozen.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government registration fee for WFOE incorporation (name reservation and business license issuance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); China does not levy a national official fee for standard enterprise registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: zero; local practice may require only technology or printing service fees, which are not official registry fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance filing and beneficial owner information pre-submission to SAMR and PBOC system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipal SAMR and the People's Bank of China beneficial owner information collection platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: zero official fee for name clearance and UBO information filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: WFOE formation legal service covering Articles of Association, shareholder resolution, registration forms, and corporate governance documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PRC law firm or licensed formation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: USD 2,000 to USD 3,500 for a standard single-shareholder WFOE with no government-approval requirement; quoted as a fixed fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille, or Chinese Consular Legalization of the foreign investor document bundle (five mandatory instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent authority in the investor's home jurisdiction; Chinese Embassy or Consulate for non-Apostille states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedules, notary tariffs, and prevailing market benchmark of USD 800 to USD 1,500 for a five-document package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign investor documents and draft WFOE constitutional documents into Simplified Chinese
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page; estimated 25 to 35 pages at USD 10 to USD 16 per page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year physical registered office commitment (serviced office or lease deposit allocation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord or serviced office provider in a city such as Shanghai, Beijing, or Shenzhen
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rent benchmark of USD 250 to USD 500 per month plus a deposit; must satisfy SAMR address rules and bank physical-inspection expectations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seals engraving (company chop, financial chop, legal representative chop, and invoice chop)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving enterprise
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local PSB tariff schedule and prevailing market benchmark of USD 100 to USD 200 for four standard seals.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-35 and 47; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 28, and 32; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2021); Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) (2021 Edition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Enterprise Registration Bureau; local Market Supervision Administration at the company's registered business address.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application Form for Company Establishment Registration (incorporating the Foreign Investment Information Report and the approved Articles of Association).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a wholly foreign-owned enterprise formed as a limited liability company under PRC law. The shareholders must subscribe the registered capital in the Articles of Association and, unless a shorter contribution period is provided in the articles, must pay the subscribed capital in full within five years after the company's establishment. No blocked escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY UNDER THE LAWS OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA.

The undersigned, constituting the first board of directors (the 'Board') of the Company, hereby convene a meeting in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association. The Board waives any separate notice period and confirms that quorum exists. All resolutions are passed unanimously.

1. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Association, and that the legal representative be authorized to execute, deliver, and perform lease agreements, landlord consents, and any utility or municipal registration documents in respect of such premises.

2. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the initial registered capital of the Company be [amount in words and figures] Renminbi, divided into [number] ordinary shares with a par value of [amount] each, and that the subscription and obligation of the sole shareholder to contribute such amount, either immediately or as scheduled in the Articles of Association, be and is hereby ratified, accepted, and recorded. The Board confirms that the paid-up contribution schedule is consistent with Article [X] of the Articles and shall be enforced by the legal representative.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open one or more corporate accounts at [bank branch], and that the legal representative, [name of officer], and [name of officer] are each authorized, jointly or singly in accordance with the signing rules approved by the Board, to execute account opening forms, sign mandate letters, give payment instructions, download banking credentials, and bind the account to the Company's tax and e-invoice system. A specimen signature card shall be kept by the corporate secretary.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed legal representative and general manager; [name] be appointed chief financial officer and corporate secretary; and [name] be appointed supervisor, each to hold office until the next general meeting or earlier removal. The legal representative is authorized to make all statutory filings, including establishment registration and seal recordation with the State Administration for Market Regulation and the Public Security Bureau.

5. IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORITY. RESOLVED, that the officers be and they hereby are directed to execute all instruments, pay all filing fees, publish notices, and undertake all lawful acts required to perfect the Company's formation and corporate governance, and to certify copies of this resolution for use before government authorities, banks, and third parties.

This resolution is effective as of [Date] and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-approval and notarization of foreign investor identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration via SAMR enterprise registration online service; Chinese diplomatic mission or legalization/apostille authority in the foreign investor's jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign sole shareholder must supply a notarized copy of its certificate of incorporation or, if the shareholder is a natural person, a notarized passport copy, each authenticated by the Chinese embassy or consulate or by the legalization/apostille procedure applicable to the jurisdiction of origin, together with a certified Chinese translation. The proposed company name must be checked through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the SAMR online name reservation module for identical or deceptively similar names. Submit the name pre-approval application with the required identity documents and the proposed Articles of Association, selecting a name containing 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.' The name reservation is valid for six months and may be renewed or adjusted before the formal company establishment application is filed.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder or notarized passport of the natural-person shareholder
Certified Chinese translation of all notarized identity documents
Power of attorney appointing the local filing agent or legal representative
Name pre-approval application form with at least three proposed company names
Draft Articles of Association
Proof of registered address intention, such as a landlord consent letter or commercial lease draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused on grounds of identical or deceptively similar names, apply again immediately with two alternative proposed names; if the refusal is alleged to be unlawful, request administrative reconsideration from the superior market supervision authority within 60 days or institute administrative litigation within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of formation dossier and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration window or SAMR online one-stop registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation, submit the unified company establishment registration application to the local Market Supervision Administration in the district where the registered office is located. Include the final Articles of Association, the notarized and legalized identity documents of the sole shareholder, the appointment instruments for the legal representative, directors, supervisor, and any manager, the proof of registered address, and the foreign investment information report that the registration authority is required to collect. The authority will verify the business scope against the Foreign Investment Negative List and will issue the business license with a unified social credit code. The company acquires legal person status upon issuance of the license.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form
Final Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder
Notarized and legalized foreign investor identity documents
Appointment instruments for legal representative, directors, supervisor, and manager
Registered address proof, including lease agreement and landlord property ownership certificate
Foreign investment information report integrated in the registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is suspended or subjected to a deficiency correction notice, correct every listed item within the specified correction period and resubmit through the same portal. If the application is formally rejected, apply for administrative reconsideration or judicial review; generally no additional state fee is charged for correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal engraving, seal recordation, and stamp control
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed seal-engraving enterprise registered with the local Public Security Bureau (PSB); PSB seal recordation window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, the legal representative must personally attend, or authorize in writing, a licensed seal-engraving enterprise registered by the Public Security Bureau to produce the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal. The engraver will scan and record the seal impressions in the PSB seal information system, generating a seal recordation certificate. The company must keep the seal register showing custody and usage. Each seal must be ordered only after verification of the legal representative's identity and the business license. For branch or contract seals, a separate application and authorization letter are required. The legal representative should confirm that all stamps are kept under dual custody if internal controls require segregation of signing authority.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Legal representative identity card or passport
Seal engraving application form signed by the legal representative
Written authorization letter if an agent attends
Name and identification number of each authorized seal custodian
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal recordation is delayed because of signature discrepancies or incomplete authorization, supplement a notarized authorization letter and resubmit the seal engraving recordation through the PSB system; a damaged or lost seal must be reported to the police and a new seal engraved after publication of the loss announcement in a municipal newspaper.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, corporate bank account opening, and accounting registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local tax service hall of the State Taxation Administration (SAT); licensed commercial bank as the depositary institution; municipal social insurance and housing fund authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after license issuance, register the company for tax purposes with the local tax service hall of the State Taxation Administration using the unified social credit code; complete the taxpayer identification setup, nominated method of accounting, e-invoice determination, and taxpayer category. Concurrently, open the company's basic deposit account at a licensed commercial bank, completing the bank's customer due diligence under the People's Bank of China anti-money-laundering rules; the bank will verify the business license, seals, shareholder identity, and beneficial owners. Register payroll, social insurance, and housing fund accounts with the relevant municipal authorities. If projected annual turnover exceeds the VAT general taxpayer threshold of RMB five million, or if voluntary registration is preferred, file the general taxpayer application with the tax authority.
required_dossiers: Business license with unified social credit code
Complete seal set, including company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal
Legal representative identity document and passport if applicable
Tax registration form for new market entities
Bank account opening application and KYC/beneficial ownership declaration
Approved board resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatories
Lease contract for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's KYC or the tax authority's registration query results in a hold, provide the requested beneficial ownership and source-of-funds evidence and request expedited processing under the applicable anti-money-laundering rules. If the tax registration is rejected for inconsistency, submit an amendment and obtain the tax registration confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment exhaust-reporting, foreign exchange registration, and annual reporting compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a designated bank as the reporting agent; Ministry of Commerce as recipient of shared foreign investment information.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon establishment, file the foreign investment information report through the integrated SAMR/National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, reporting the foreign investor's identity, business scope, capital subscription schedule, and ultimate beneficial owner. Verify that the scope is not in the prohibited or restricted categories of the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List). Complete the foreign exchange receipt and capital account registration through the selected bank as the proceeding agent for the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, if paid-in capital is to be remitted or the company expects to receive foreign exchange. Finally, update the company's annual reporting and beneficial owner information with SAMR through the publicity system. All forms must be signed by the legal representative or authorized agent.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment information report filed through the integrated SAMR reporting system
Final business license copy
Capital subscription schedule reflected in the Articles of Association
Beneficial ownership declaration and ultimate shareholder structure chart
Capital account registration application submitted through the PRC bank
Final certified copy of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment information report or SAFE registration is queried due to misclassification, amend the business scope by filing a change registration with SAMR and resubmit the foreign investment information report. Any negative-list non-conformity must be cured by divestiture or renewed compliance filing before further reporting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The registrable scope is pure digital software development and mobile utility application publishing under ISIC 6201; no industrial licensing board triggers for physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The mobile utility application is distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play using an App_Store_Freemium model, and the entity does not operate physical industrial premises requiring a dedicated operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable. The project involves no construction of physical works, no manufacturing installations, no chemical operations, and no warehousing, and therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment report or environmental registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no quantified wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or stack emission thresholds applicable to a pure software development company with a general office lease.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No special civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval is required for the pure digital/consulting scope, beyond ordinary commercial building fire safety compliance in the leased office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Taxation platform) accessible through the STA national portal at https://www.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) incorporated in mainland China, the statutory TIN equivalence is established through the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) upon business license issuance. The WFOE must complete initial tax registration with the competent local STA office within 30 days of incorporation; the tax registration is completed automatically in the STA taxpayer master database using the USCC as the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT taxpayer identifier. The entity must subsequently complete tax-type recognition, invoice-printing/quota authorization, and VAT general taxpayer registration or small-scale taxpayer election. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has no registered Chinese establishment but derives China-source income, the non-resident entity or its Chinese withholding agent must apply for a non-resident enterprise tax code with the competent STA office at the place where the payer is located; this code is used exclusively for corporate income tax withholding and VAT/surrogate collection obligations. The WFOE itself, as a Chinese-resident limited liability company, cannot elect to be treated as a disregarded branch and must obtain its Chinese TIN/USCC through the SAMR-ST integrated registration process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (China does not provide a check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid mismatch election mechanism; a WFOE is mandatorily taxable as a resident enterprise at the entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; transfer pricing, thin capitalization, and controlled foreign corporation rules may impose compulsory adjustments but do not constitute elective classification regimes).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) administered by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All Chinese legal entities must complete tax registration within 30 days of obtaining their business license; there is no turnover threshold for taxpayer registration. The mandatory economic turnover threshold for VAT general taxpayer classification is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (approximately USD equivalent); once this threshold is exceeded, the WFOE must register as a VAT general taxpayer and may not retroactively remain a small-scale taxpayer. For enterprises with annual taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000, small-scale taxpayer treatment applies at the current reduced levy rate (historically 3%, with temporary preferential rates at 1% applicable from time to time), but the WFOE may elect general taxpayer status if permanent establishment, export refund, or input VAT credit requirements justify doing so.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China enforces a national all-digital electronic invoice regime through the STA's Full-Link Digital Electronic Invoice system; all VAT invoices must be issued through the Electronic Tax Administration platform, and invoice data are transmitted in real time to the STA Golden Tax System (Golden Tax IV) for central validation, digital stamping, and allocation of a tax control number. Taxpayers must integrate e-invoicing APIs with their ERP/billing systems for special VAT invoices where required. Physical paper invoices are being phased out in favor of digital invoices; all invoice issuance, red-letter reversals, and statement filing obligations are subject to real-time fiscal clearance and anti-fraud matching against the STA's central tax-control database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to VAT general taxpayer exported goods: the goods must be customs-cleared as exports, physically leave Chinese customs territory, and the export proceeds must be repatriated into China through lawful foreign exchange channels; the VAT rate is set at 0% with corresponding refund of input VAT. For qualifying cross-border services and intangible products, including offshore software and mobile application licensing services, zero-rating eligibility requires that the recipient is a non-resident enterprise or individual, the service is consumed wholly outside mainland China, the sales contract, payment flow, and foreign exchange settlement documentation prove offshore delivery, and the service does not involve domestic use in China. The WFOE must maintain a complete export/offshore transaction dossier to substantiate the zero-rated treatment and must declare the zero-rated export sales in the VAT return under the applicable export tax refund/zero-rating line item. If an app sale through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing is structured as a distribution of digital software to foreign end users, the WFOE must evidence the offshore recipient identity, the place of consumption, and repatriation of net proceeds to China through the designated foreign exchange bank before applying the 0% rate or the export VAT refund.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form (Export Goods Declaration Report) duly stamped and released by China Customs
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / International Express Waybill evidencing physical departure of exported goods from Chinese customs territory
Commercial invoices and export contract/purchase order showing the foreign buyer and delivery basis

SAFE Export Proceeds Verification Certificate or bank-issued Foreign Exchange Receipt and Settlement Confirmation evidencing lawful repatriation of export consideration into the Chinese WFOE bank account
Customs-approved inspection/quarantine or commodity inspection documents when the exported goods are subject to statutory inspections
Digital electronic VAT special invoice or export invoice linkage record connecting the customs declaration to the VAT general taxpayer account
Packing list, insurance certificate, and freight documentation aligned with incoterms and cargo value declared in the customs export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly audit export tax refund and zero-rating claims using cross-matching of customs declarations, foreign exchange receipts, invoice data, and VAT return filings. If any mandatory customs document, export proceeds remittance record, or offshore consumption evidentiary document is missing, unverified, inconsistent, or falsified, the claimed zero rate is revoked and all previously refunded or credited VAT is clawed back with statutory late-payment surcharge. Fraudulent export VAT claims are penalized under Article 63 of the Law on Administration of Tax Collection with an administrative fine of 50% to 500% of the refunded tax amount, and the taxpayer may be stripped of export tax refund qualifications and listed in the tax integrity blacklist. Where the false export refund constitutes a crime, Criminal Law Article 204 for fraudulent export VAT refunds imposes severe criminal liability, including imprisonment of up to life imprisonment in aggravated cases, forfeiture of the illegal refunded amount, and monetary fines. The WFOE must therefore retain its export/offshore transaction file for at least five years and be prepared to produce original customs declarations, banking/SAFE receipts, and foreign exchange repatriation evidence during a tax audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the direct supervision of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with convertibility achieved for current account items but strict oversight over capital account items. The Renminbi is freely convertible for trade in goods and services, profit remittance, and current operational payments provided that a genuine underlying transaction evidencing the PRC bank is obtained and that the bank performs the 'real-instruction and real-deal' compliance review. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity injections, cross-border loans, bond issuance, and outbound investments, require SAFE registration, approval, or post-event reporting. A WFOE is permitted to convert registered capital into local currency via a capital account using the Onshore Capital Account system, but such funds cannot be used outside the approved business scope. Profit distribution, dividends, and royalties remitted abroad are considered current account items; still, a corporate income tax withholding certificate, audited financial statements for the distributable profit, and a board resolution are mandatory, and banks transfer remittances after verifying that the amount does not exceed the distributable surplus. There is no blanket surrender requirement on export proceeds; enterprises may retain foreign exchange in their current account foreign currency deposits or settle in RMB according to commercial needs. However, all receipts must be repatriated and duly recorded in the bank's balance of payments system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE framework, the mandatory export surrender ratio has been abolished. A WFOE receiving export proceeds arising from digital app sales is not required to convert any mandated percentage into RMB; the entity may retain foreign currency in its current account foreign exchange deposit account or sell it to a licensed onshore bank. Nevertheless, export proceeds must be repatriated to the PRC within the regulatory collection and verification timeline, generally not exceeding 180 days from the date of export declaration or the relevant payment trigger, unless an extension is approved by the bank and SAFE through the cross-border collection verification system. All export receipts must be reported to SAFE under the balance of payments statistical reporting rules with the proper trade or service item code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not legally permitted to open corporate accounts or execute foreign exchange transactions on behalf of a mainland China WFOE. Chinese banking law and SAFE regulations require all onshore corporate foreign receipts and payments to be settled through licensed commercial banks operating within the SAFE foreign exchange monitoring system. An unauthorized offshore EMI would expose the entity to penalties under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, the Anti-Money Laundering Law, and the PBOC's Rules on the Administration of Payment Services. Some licensed PBOC payment institutions may offer cross-border e-commerce collection solutions, but these institutions must hold a valid Cross-Border RMB Settlement qualification and a Payment Business License. The viability of using a pure fintech EMI is therefore Very Low, and the WFOE should structure its collection rails through a licensed domestic commercial bank or a qualified third-party payment institution engaged by the bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In mainland China, a WFOE corporate account opening generally requires the statutory legal representative to appear physically at a bank branch for an in-person identity interview and signing session. The legal representative must present original passports, the foreigner's work permit or residence permit if applicable, the notarised certificate of incorporation and business license, the tax registration certificate, and company chops. Remote consular proxy opening is not commonly accepted by Tier-1 banks; certain branches may allow video-conference identity verification for beneficial owners who are not statutory representatives, but the statutory representative or a properly authorised senior officer with power of attorney must still attend a branch interview. For non-resident legal representatives, the bank's compliance committee may require an additional live video call and certified copies of board resolutions before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal representative or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-resident with multiple passports, tax residencies, or a high-risk jurisdiction connection, triggering enhanced sanctions and PEP screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Must submit a comprehensive client information file including certified passport copies and valid visas, a tax residence certificate from all applicable jurisdictions, a full employment and residential history, a notarised negative media report from a reputable screening vendor, documentary evidence of source of wealth such as pay slips, sale deeds, share transfer agreements, inherited assets, and multi-year tax returns, together with a signed declaration that neither the legal representative nor the UBO is a PEP, sanctions target, or conduit for a third party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered capital injection originates from a related holding company domiciled in a secrecy or shell-haven jurisdiction or flows through a pooled account, raising round-tripping and capital laundering suspicions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a capital source questionnaire and statutory undertaking, a consolidated ownership chart from the ultimate individual owners to the paying parent, audited financial statements of the remitting entity, bank statements for the last 12 to 24 months tracing the exact funding path, a certified SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration form, the shareholders' agreement and board resolution approving the equity contribution, and a local Chinese certified public accountant (CPA) capital verification report after the funds arrive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The digital mobile utility business generates high volumes of micro-transactions through Apple App Store and Google Play without traditional export customs declarations, making the trade rationale difficult to validate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed app store developer agreements with Apple and Google, export payout settlement statements showing aggregated net proceeds, transaction-level ledger extracts and reconciliation reports, backend developer console screenshots demonstrating active users and transactions, independent audit trail from the app store payout gateway to the WFOE's receiving bank, and a contractual explanation for any fees, commissions, or refunds that affect the net remittance amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regular rapid disbursements to foreign cloud hosting providers, marketing platforms, and software developers create an outbound RMB to foreign currency velocity pattern that could be mistaken for trade mis-invoicing or capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a board-approved treasury policy and payment calendar, original contracts or service-level agreements for cloud hosting, advertising and development services, invoices and delivery acceptances, tax withholding certificates as required, SAFE service trade registration documentation, and confirmation letters from the ultimate service providers explaining the necessity, scope, and remuneration basis of each cross-border payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must first complete SAFE FDI registration through a designated onshore bank and receive a Foreign Exchange Registration Business Form. The inward capital contribution should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 with the remitter name exactly matching the foreign shareholder and the wire narration stating 'Investment Equity Contribution' or 'Capital Injection'. The receiving bank will apply the payment to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital account under the SAFE purpose code for direct investment. Upon credit confirmation, the amount cannot be settled into RMB unless the bank verifies the intended use against the approved business scope and applicable capital account payment policy. A local CPA then issues a formal Capital Verification Report, confirming that the injection complies with the registered capital commitments and the Company Law. Any subsequent repatriation of capital or profit requires the bank to validate the previous capital verification report, the audited financial statements, and the relevant tax settlement certificates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational trade disbursements, the WFOE should use standard SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for direct foreign currency payments to suppliers, contractors, and digital service providers. For inventory or software licensing acquisitions where the counterparty requires documentary security, a commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 is preferable, coupled with presentation of invoices, transport or delivery evidence, and inspection documents. Documentary Collections under URC522 may be used for lower-risk relationships, allowing the bank to transmit shipping and payment documents without undertaking to pay. All outward remittances must be supported by the underlying contract, invoice, tax payment certificates if applicable, and the appropriate service trade or goods trade purpose codes. For reconstructed payments through app store platforms, the WFOE should instruct the licensed bank to cite the original app store settlement reference in the MT103 narrative to maintain a clear audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB forward contracts with a licensed commercial bank, executed only against genuine underlying current account or capital account exposure and constrained by the SAFE 'real needs' principle

Cross-currency swaps and interest rate swaps permitted for hedging the principal and interest of foreign-currency denominated cross-border working capital loans, provided the loan agreement and SAFE registration are evidenced
FX options and option combinations (zero-cost collars) used solely for risk hedging on projected app store revenues and known overseas expense obligations, with no speculative open positions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally prohibited for onshore corporate clients; any offshore CNH NDF intended by the parent group must be structured through an offshore licensed bank and cannot be booked or settled through the mainland WFOE without SAFE approval, which would be extremely difficult to obtain for a pure treasury hedge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local market supervision administrations through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June of the year following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish within the statutory window places the company on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; continued non-compliance for 3 years leads to inclusion on the List of Seriously Law-Breaking and Untrustworthy Enterprises, credit blacklisting, targeted regulatory inspection, and eventual administrative revocation of the business license; false annual-report information may attract fines and personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and local commerce departments, collected through the SAMR annual-report system and shared with market-regulation authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June of the year following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the prescribed correction notice is not honored within the statutory period, a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000) may be imposed; false, concealed, or misleading investment information may also trigger additional credit and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return, including financial statement schedules, related-party disclosures, and transfer pricing documentation if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local tax service bureau and electronic taxpayer system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the tax year, within 5 months after the close of the annual accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an order to rectify and a penalty of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; unpaid tax carries a 0.05% daily overdue surcharge and a penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the underpaid tax; persistent non-filing can lead to compulsory tax enforcement, invoice restrictions, and joint credit discipline measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Audit Report of the WFOE annual financial statements, issued by an accounting firm registered with the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants (CICPA), and submitted to shareholders, the tax authorities, and relevant financing or foreign-exchange banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No separate government filing of the audit report is generally required; the audit report is submitted to the shareholders and board, attached to the Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return, and made available to SAMR, MOFCOM, and foreign-exchange banks upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must cover the preceding 1 January to 31 December statutory year and be completed in sufficient time to accompany the annual CIT final settlement by 31 May; it must also be ready before any profit distribution or shareholder approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and audit annual financial statements as required by PRC Company Law constitutes a statutory violation; distributors cannot lawfully declare or pay dividends, tax filings may be rejected or selected for comprehensive audit or inspection, and the company may be ordered to rectify, fined by fiscal or corporate authorities, and subjected to credit sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every company must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by an accounting firm registered in China; there is no minimum balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption for a WFOE limited liability company. The audit obligation is universal. A compulsory certified CPA audit is therefore triggered by the mere existence of the incorporated WFOE, regardless of zero revenue, small headcount, or low asset value; additional audit or review obligations may be imposed by tax authorities, SAMR, foreign-exchange banks, or investors for annual returns, capital remittances, loans, or transaction support.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), as issued by the Ministry of Finance of the PRC, substantially converged with IFRS; a WFOE so qualified may use the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but statutory standalone financial statements are prepared under PRC accounting standards rather than IFRS. IFRS statements may only be prepared as supplementary group reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PRC law does not maintain a separate annual UBO certificate for ordinary WFOEs. Beneficial-ownership information is captured through the Foreign Investment Information Annual Report due by 30 June each year, which discloses the foreign investor and its actual controller or beneficial owner, and through the statutory shareholders register maintained at the registered office. Any shareholding transfer, change of beneficial ownership, or control change must be reported to MOFCOM or SAMR as a change report within 30 calendar days of the event; the shareholders register and board minutes must also be updated contemporaneously.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Supervisors and Senior Management
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Minute Book of Shareholders Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,500 per year for a compliant registered business address and local secretarial or registered-agent services in a major first-tier city; premium serviced premises may exceed this range.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 4,500 per year for a typical small WFOE performing mobile utility app development and freemium distribution, assuming standard intercompany transactions and no full transfer-pricing report; fees increase with transaction volume, group reporting deadlines, or multi-entity consolidation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard PRC Corporate Income Tax (CIT) is 25% under Article 4 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law (EITL). The mobile utility app developer may qualify for: (i) Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential treatment through 2027 where annual taxable income is at or below RMB 3 million, employees at or below 300, and total assets at or below RMB 500 million, producing a 5% effective rate; (ii) a 15% reduced rate for High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) certification; (iii) a 10% rate for key national software enterprises certified by the relevant authorities; (iv) a 100% super-deduction (200% total deduction) of qualifying R&D expenses until 2027; (v) exemption or incentive for technical transfer income up to RMB 5 million; and (vi) potentially a 15% rate in designated preferential zones such as the Hainan Free Trade Port. A standard WFOE outside those incentives remains taxed at 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form: PRC Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Class A) - Form A100000 plus affiliated schedules; electronic filing is mandatory on the State Taxation Administration's Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final CIT return is due by May 31 (five months) after the fiscal year-end of December 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from Apple App Store and Google Play in-app purchases, subscriptions, premium version sales, in-app advertising, and license/maintenance fees, net of value-added tax (VAT) and statutory returns/discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE with non-resident parents, the WFOE is the Chinese enterprise income taxpayer on its worldwide income if it is resident. All China-market app-store revenue must be accrued and reported in Box 1; profit cannot be shifted to offshore app-store intermediaries or foreign shell subsidiaries. The taxpayer must reconcile Apple IAP and Google Play Billing reports to the filed revenue line. Omission of Chinese downloads and in-app purchases from foreign-affiliated distribution agreements will constitute a false return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of app development and maintenance, including programmer and quality assurance salaries, cloud hosting, server fees, third-party software licenses, and amortization of capitalized app development expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs invoiced by non-resident related parties for cloud infrastructure, code libraries, algorithms, or remote software services must satisfy the arm's length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing (TP) documentation. Any expense with insufficient economic benefit or without actual service delivery will be disallowed and may be reclassified as a deemed dividend or royalty to the non-resident group, triggering withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge based on the actual VAT paid on digital sales; VAT itself is excluded from this line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Digital app sales through Apple/Google are generally services taxable at 6% VAT; if the WFOE qualifies as a small-scale VAT payer, a lower VAT levy may apply. The CIT return must not reflect VAT as a deductible corporate expense, and no adjustment is made for non-resident users who download the app from offshore app-store portals. The WFOE must file VAT separately with State Taxation Administration portals.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: User-acquisition advertising, pay-per-install marketing, app-store optimisation, localisation, promotions, attribution software, and other sales and marketing expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Marketing services purchased from a foreign parent or group service company must be substantiated by a written contract, actual delivery evidence, and an arm's length fee analysis. Chinese tax authorities frequently disallow intercompany marketing fees that duplicate shareholder-department services. If denied, the add-back may be recharacterised as a distribution to the non-resident shareholder, subject to 10% dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative headcount costs, office rent, insurance, professional fees, regulatory costs, enterprise software, and group-management service charges allocated to the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shared group costs from a non-resident management company are deductible only where the services are actually received, are not duplicative of shareholder services, and the fee reflects the benefit test under SAT TP circulars. A documented service agreement and allocation key must exist before payment. Merely having a 'cost plus' invoice without local substance creates a TP adjustment risk and treaty-benefit exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest and financing costs, foreign exchange losses, bank charges, loan arrangement fees, and intercompany borrowing expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest deductions on loans from non-resident shareholders are subject to the thin-capitalisation ratio: for a non-financial enterprise, debt-to-equity cannot exceed 2:1. Interest on over-leveraged intercompany debt is non-deductible. The WFOE must also withhold the statutory 10% non-resident interest withholding tax, or an applicable treaty-reduced rate, on gross interest paid to the overseas lender. A valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration are required for treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Line 7 (Investment income and non-operating income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends, royalties, gains, and other non-operating income earned by the WFOE during the year, including amounts from overseas affiliates or foreign financial investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a resident Chinese enterprise are generally deductible/exempt, but dividends from non-resident companies are taxable and may be eligible for foreign-tax credit. For a mobile utility app WFOE, any royalties received from offshore related users or app-store partners must be declared as taxable income. Income from a BVI or Hong Kong IP-holding sub cannot be excluded merely because remitted abroad; the Chinese-resident WFOE must prove that the true economic activity supporting the income occurred outside China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Related party transaction declaration schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all related-party relationships and transactions, including parent entity identity, volumes of tangible/intangible transfers, services, financing, pricing methods, benchmarking data, and local-file/master-file maintenance status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must attach the annual related-party business report whenever any related-party transaction exists, regardless of amount. Non-resident parent details, contracts, and TP selection must match the China Local File and Master File. Failure to file this schedule is itself a violation under the Tax Administration Collection Law and draws administrative fines plus forced filing; it also operates as a red flag for profit-stripping audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late CIT return filing: RMB 2,000 penalty, increasing to RMB 10,000 for aggravated cases under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Collection Law; late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day of unpaid tax under Article 32. Understatement or omission causing tax evasion: penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63, daily late surcharges, and criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law where the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and more than 10% of the tax otherwise payable; imprisonment is up to seven years. False TP declarations additionally expose the entity to special tax investigation and 5% annual interest on adjusted tax differences.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory non-resident dividend WHT on outbound dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise under EITL Article 27 and related implementing notices; 20% for non-resident individuals. Bilateral double-taxation agreements may reduce the corporate rate to 5% for qualifying substantial shareholdings (generally 25% or more) or 10% for portfolio holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must claim treaty relief before payment by: (1) obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) in the jurisdiction of residence; (2) submitting to the WFOE as withholding agent a signed Treaty Entitlement Application (and applicable forms) that discloses the beneficial owner, direct shareholding, commercial rationale, purpose, and absence of a conduit arrangement; (3) providing the TRC, shareholding ledger, and underlying commercial contract to be filed in the Electronic Tax Bureau withholding system. If the reduced rate is approved before remittance, the WFOE withholds at the treaty rate; if not approved, it must withhold the statutory 10% at payment, and the non-resident may apply for a refund within three years. The relief is denied when the recipient lacks beneficial ownership, performs no business activity, or is a shell without economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: China-source royalties and interest paid to non-residents bear a statutory 10% WHT. Royalties may also be subject to VAT at 6% and surcharge of 12% of that VAT, unless specially exempt. Treaty relief, when substantiated with a TRC and beneficial ownership evidence, commonly reduces interest WHT to 10% or 5% for financial institutions and royalty WHT to 10% or 5% depending on the treaty and the nature of the intellectual property. Reservation, withholding, and reporting must be done on the non-resident enterprise withholding return contemporaneously with payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A China Local File must be prepared by a WFOE whose annual related-party transactions any single category exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible-property transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible-property transfers; RMB 100 million for financial-asset transfers; RMB 40 million for related-party services transfers; or RMB 20 million for other related-party transactions. A Master File is additionally required when the taxpayer's annual aggregate related-party transaction amount exceeds RMB 10 billion. The related-party transaction disclosure schedules must be filed annually without any threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the economic substance doctrine through EITL Articles 46-47, Article 120 of the Implementation Regulations, and tax-treaty anti-abuse rules. The GAAR permits the tax authority to recharacterise structures with no reasonable commercial purpose and to deny treaty benefits to conduit companies. For the WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for the mobile utility app must take place in China: software source-code development, server management, data analytics, user-experience decision-making, pricing strategy, and operational risk control. If these functions are actually performed in mainland China while profits are booked to a Hong Kong or Singapore affiliate lacking substance, the Chinese tax authority will reallocate income back to the WFOE and may apply the GAAR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via sham transfer pricing and offshore profit stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells its developed mobile app algorithm and Chinese user database on paper to a BVI affiliate at a grossly underpriced value, then pays the affiliate inflated royalty fees for the use of that same intellectual property, thereby stripping PRC-source operating profits offshore and reporting near-zero taxable income in China despite substantial Chinese sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The State Taxation Administration may apply EITL Article 41 to recompute the revenue at an arm's length price, impose a TP adjustment with 5% annual interest, levy a 50%-500% penalty under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Collection Law, and refer the case to the criminal system under Criminal Law Article 201 when the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and 10% of the tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the de facto controller are jointly and severally liable for the restituted tax and penalties if they directed the sham TP arrangement. Tax authorities may blacklist each executive for travel control under Article 44 of the Tax Administration Collection Law, preventing departure from mainland China until taxes and penalties are settled. Civil judgments can attach personal bank accounts and equity interests. Willful participation carries imprisonment of up to seven years and a personal criminal fine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Willful failure to withhold and remit non-resident withholding tax on outbound dividends, royalties, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays tens of millions of RMB in dividends, software royalties, and intercompany interest to its non-resident parent without filing non-resident withholding returns, without obtaining TRCs, and without remitting the statutory 10% WHT to the Chinese State tax authority; the payments are routed through Apple/Google billing to create the appearance that no China-source income exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 69 of the Tax Administration Collection Law, the WFOE as withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld tax, a penalty from 50% to 300% of the unwithheld amount, and daily late surcharges at 0.05%. If the unremitted sum exceeds RMB 50,000, the case may be prosecuted as tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment for up to seven years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signed the remittance and instructed the accountant not to withhold is personally liable to pay the under-withheld tax and penalties out of personal assets. The court may freeze personal bank accounts, attach personal property, and issue a travel ban (blacklisting) against the director and the finance officer. A criminal conviction results in imprisonment from five to seven years for aggravated fraud and disqualification from acting as director in any PRC company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Operating as an economic-substance shell and claiming DTA relief through a conduit shareholder
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is registered as a mainland China entity but has no office, no employees in China, no local board meetings, and no CIGA; all material activities and management decisions occur offshore, and a Hong Kong intermediary entity is inserted as the nominal recipient of Chinese dividends and royalties solely to obtain a treaty rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority applies the GAAR under EITL Articles 47 and 120, disregards the shell/conduit arrangement, reclassifies the income as China-source income taxable at 25%, and denies treaty benefits under the beneficial-ownership tests and anti-abuse provisions of tax conventions. Financial penalties include the full reassessed tax, 5% annual interest on overdue amounts, and a 50%-500% evasive penalty under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Collection Law. Criminal exposure arises if the taxpayer files false treaty-benefit declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face corporate-veil piercing under Company Law principles where they abuse limited-liability status to evade compulsory tax obligations. Personal civil liability includes restitution of the entire underpaid State tax plus interest and penalties, enforced against personal bank accounts, shares, and real estate. The director is also placed on the tax exit-control blacklist, and the criminal path under Criminal Law Article 201 can result in imprisonment of up to seven years and an individual criminal fine.
